title: Implementation (reference project): CAN transport and the periodic BMS-state frame the reference project relies on for state publication, with a proposed request-refusal publication the pinned source does not contain

standards_mappings.reference: Part 6, Clause 9 (this record is a code location, not a verification record)
standards_mappings.rationale: States where the code for the reference project's communication path is. Makes no claim that it was verified and asserts no ASIL classification for the real product.
There is no software design artefact for the CAN transport in either profile. The gap is declared rather than closed by attaching this module to an unrelated design.

revision_history.author: sw_engineer
revision_history.description: First issue. The reference project's system requirements FB2-SYS-SYR-000007 and -000008 need a communication element to exist in the graph for the chain from the designs to code to be traversable, and the pinned source's CAN transport and BMS-state frame are the code the reference project would reuse for them. Authored with the refusal path that SYR-000007 requires and the source does not have, declared as a proposal.

proposed_location.why_not_in_source: The reference project's system requirement FB2-SYS-SYR-000007 requires the item to act on a state request from the vehicle control unit only when the request is consistent with its own safety evaluation, and to refuse the request and publish the refusal with its reason where it is not. Its acceptance criteria make refusal diagnosability 100% of refusals. The pinned BMS-state transmit frame contains no refusal field and no refusal reason: a search of the file for refus returns no occurrence, and the frame is built by CANTX_BuildBmsStateMessage from the item's own state only. The application's request check BMS_CheckStateRequest (bms.c:347-366) does return BMS_ILLEGAL_REQUEST or BMS_ALREADY_INITIALIZED for a request it will not accept, but nothing publishes that return value to the vehicle control unit, so the requirement's diagnosable-refusal criterion has no code path in the product. The proposed symbol is a new element the reference project would have to add; it does not exist in the product and is not presented as if it did.

implements.relationship: No software design artefact in either profile describes the CAN transport, so there is no design for this element to implement and no implements link is asserted. What the module does, read from the pinned source and verified there: CAN_ConfigureRxMailboxesForExtendedIdentifiers (can.c:272-565) programs the peripheral's extended-identifier receive mailboxes from the vendor configuration constants whose provenance the file's own comment records as the TI HALCoGen HL_can.c of 11-Dec-2018; CAN_RxInterrupt (643-692) reads a frame, accepts it only when no data was lost and the queues exist, derives the identifier width from the mailbox number, and enqueues it while reporting the queue-full condition as a diagnosis entry on both outcomes; CAN_ReadRxBuffer (1015-1031) drains that queue and dispatches to the registered callback for the matching node, identifier and width; CAN_PeriodicTransmit (694-744) empties the transmit queue and services the periodic frames. The frame the reference project relies on for state publication is CANTX_BmsState (can_cbs_tx_f_bms-state.c:427-454), which builds the payload in CANTX_BuildBmsStateMessage (187-424) from the item's own state, including the substate read through BMS_GetSubstate at line 202 and a system-monitoring timing check through CANTX_AnySysMonTimingIssueDetected at 171-185. So the element provides transport, buffering, dispatch and the periodic state frame, and does not provide the refusal publication its consumer requirement needs.
implements.design_gap_reason: Neither profile contains a software design artefact for the CAN transport. Both profiles' three software design records cover the AFE driver, the SOA module and the contactor driver, none of which describes CAN transport or the vehicle-facing interface. The as_is profile records the same gap in deviation FB2-SW-DEV-000007. Attaching this module to an existing design would assert communication design coverage neither profile has, so design_artifact_id is null and no implements link is created. This is a typed leaf exception under master prompt section 13.

realises_requirements.how_realised: Partially. The publication half is realised: CANTX_BmsState builds and transmits a periodic frame carrying the item's own state, which is the mechanism by which mode is published. The limit-publication half is not realised by this element - charge and discharge limits are carried by different frames in the same callback directory - and the refusal half is not realised at all and is declared in proposed_location as not_in_source. The reference project's realisation of this requirement is therefore incomplete at revision 1 on two of its four acceptance criteria.

behaviours.description: Programs the peripheral's receive mailboxes for extended identifiers from literal constants copied from the vendor HAL configuration, the origin of the in-source MISRA deviation recorded against this function.
Receive interrupt: reads a frame, accepts it only when no data was lost and the queues exist, derives the identifier width from the mailbox number, and enqueues it.
Reports the receive queue's full condition as a diagnosis entry on both the accepted and the refused outcome, so a dropped frame is distinguishable from a delivered one.
Drains the receive queue in task context and invokes the callback registered for each frame's node, identifier and identifier width.
Empties the transmit queue and services the configured periodic messages when periodic transmission is enabled.

Builds and transmits the periodic BMS-state frame from the item's own state, including its substate and a system-monitoring timing check. This is the publication mechanism the reference project's state-publication requirement relies on, and it carries no refusal information.

concurrency_and_isr_context.shared_state: ftsk_canRxQueue, which the interrupt fills through the FromIsr queue API and CAN_ReadRxBuffer drains through the non-Isr one.
The same receive queue, and the transmit path the periodic frame uses. CANTX_BuildBmsStateMessage reads the item's state through accessor calls rather than through shared storage.

guard.statement: This record describes the communication element the hypothetical reference project would reuse, and declares, as a proposal, the refusal publication its own state-publication requirement needs and the pinned source does not contain. It is not evidence that FB2-SYS-SYR-000007 is met: two of that requirement's four acceptance criteria have no code path here, and no frame was sent or received to establish anything. It confers no production authority, no verification credit and no human approval, and it asserts nothing about the real foxBMS product's safety classification.

evidence_status.method: Every code_location was read at the pinned commit with 'git show 308028fb:path'; each content_hash is that pinned blob's sha256. For the four can.c locations the hash equals the value the corresponding pre-existing source-registry anchor already carries; for the two locations in the BMS-state callback file no anchor exists and the hash was computed at the pin for this record. Each named symbol was confirmed to occur inside its recorded line_range at the pin and each range was confirmed within the file. The can.c spans were cross-read against 'graft skeleton src/app/driver/can/can.c' and the callback spans against 'graft skeleton src/app/driver/can/cbs/tx-cyclic/can_cbs_tx_f_bms-state.c'.
limitations: The proposed_location entry names a symbol that DOES NOT EXIST in the pinned source and is not a source anchor. It is a proposal for the hypothetical project and is recorded here precisely so that it cannot be mistaken for a verified location or for an implemented refusal path.

The absence of a refusal field in the BMS-state frame was established by reading the file at the pinned commit and searching it for refus, which returns no occurrence. It is an absence claim about this file and is stated as such.

The mailbox numbers, register masks and identifier shift constants inside CAN_ConfigureRxMailboxesForExtendedIdentifiers are deliberately not reproduced here, because their authoritative definition is the external vendor configuration file this corpus cannot read; restating them would create an unverifiable second copy of a register map.
Behaviour was verified by reading the code. No CAN frame was sent or received and no timing measurement exists in this corpus.
All five files are unmodified between the pin and the working tree, so the same ranges and hashes hold for the checked-out files.

provenance_note: The three anchors referenced are the same pre-existing anchors the as_is CAN record uses, because both profiles describe the same real source. The two BMS-state callback locations have no anchor and none was created; they are named in this record's code_locations with their own pinned content hashes so that they remain independently verifiable without extending the shared anchor set.
